data.label: Detect New Opportunity
data.description: Trigger when a new sales opportunity is created in the CRM.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger based on a CRM create event. No AI, ML, or language understanding is required; simple webhook/event subscription logic is sufficient.

data.label: Validate Opportunity Fields
data.description: Verify the deal has an assigned owner, stated dollar value, and target close date.
data.rationale: This is pure rule-based validation of required fields. It can be implemented with straightforward if/then checks and field presence/format validation, which fits L0.

data.label: Flag Missing Data
data.description: If required opportunity fields are missing, flag the record for correction.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic downstream action triggered by validation failure. It only applies a rule-based flag and does not involve prediction or language generation.

data.label: Fetch Historical Win Rates
data.description: Look up win-rate data for similar deals to provide historical context.
data.rationale: At minimum, this is a deterministic database lookup or filtered aggregation over historical records. L0 is enough if the lookup criteria are fixed; no ML is necessary to retrieve similar-deal statistics.

data.label: Assign Confidence Score
data.description: Evaluate the opportunity against historical data and assign a deal-stage confidence score.
data.rationale: This step goes beyond fixed rules because it estimates a confidence score from historical patterns among similar deals. That is a supervised prediction task (regression/classification) and fits L1. L0 alone would not generalize well across deal patterns and win-rate variation.

data.label: Check High-Confidence Threshold
data.description: Determine whether the opportunity is high-confidence and above 50000 dollars.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic threshold check using the computed confidence score and deal value. It is classic rule-based branching with no AI requirement.

data.label: Schedule Proposal Prep Meeting
data.description: Automatically schedule a proposal-prep meeting with the sales engineering team for eligible deals.
data.rationale: Scheduling the meeting requires interacting with external systems such as a calendar or scheduling API. The orchestration is deterministic, but the step is tool-augmented because it performs an action in another system rather than only computing locally.

data.label: Monitor Deal Activity
data.description: Detect opportunities that have stalled for more than 14 days without activity.
data.rationale: This is deterministic time-based logic using last-activity timestamps and a fixed 14-day threshold. It can be implemented with simple date comparisons and scheduled checks at L0.

data.label: Flag for Manager Review
data.description: Flag stalled opportunities for sales manager review.
data.rationale: This is a straightforward deterministic status update/flagging action based on the stalled-deal condition. No learning or language processing is required.

data.label: Draft Re-engagement Email
data.description: Create a re-engagement email draft for the rep to send on stalled deals.
data.rationale: This step requires generating a natural-language email draft. A single LLM can produce the message self-contained without external tools, which makes it L3 rather than rule-based or simple NLP.

data.label: Record Stage Transitions
data.description: Log every stage transition with timestamp and triggering event.
data.rationale: This is deterministic audit logging: append the timestamp, event name, and transition details to a record store. It is pure L0 logging/serialization logic.

data.label: if confidence high and value > 50000

data.condition: stalled-deal monitoring runs alongside confidence-based routing
data.label: in parallel

data.label: if stalled > 14 days

message: Overall this workflow is predominantly L0 deterministic automation, with one L1 scoring step for historical win-rate prediction, one L3 step for drafting a re-engagement email, and one L4 tool-augmented scheduling step that interacts with external calendar/CRM systems. No multi-agent orchestration is required.

workflow.workflowBrief: When a new sales opportunity is created in the CRM, verify that the deal has an assigned owner, a stated dollar value, and a target close date. Check the opportunity against historical win-rate data for similar deals and assign a deal-stage confidence score. For high-confidence deals above 50000 dollars, automatically schedule a proposal-prep meeting with the sales engineering team. For deals that have stalled more than 14 days without activity, flag the opportunity for sales manager review and draft a re-engagement email for the rep. Record every stage transition with timestamp and triggering event.
